sourceSentences: Yone dashes a fixed distance in the target direction, including through terrain, discarding his body and entering Spirit Form for 5 seconds.
Yone's body is untargetable and is sent the same distance behind the cast location, though not through terrain, and is reclaimed when Soul Unbound ends.
The dash can cross terrain.
Blinking during Mortal Steel's cast with two stacks of Gathering Storm (after the cast time) will end the dash prematurely but enemies in range of Yone at the new location are affected.
All three of the thrust, whirlwind and dash roll for a critical strike on each individual target hit.
The automatic recast is delayed if Yone is winding up a basic attack or is unable to recast Soul Unbound under any circumstances, which includes if he cannot move or cast abilities.
If Yone uses Mortal Steel at two Gathering Storm stacks to delay Soul Unbound's automatic recast, he will be able to basic attack once in a short time period before the automatic recast triggers.
The marks do not store damage from items, runes, summoner spells, and other effects, excluding damage that inherits champion source.
The marks will not store damage dealt to shields.
There is no attack time-out between alternating swords. It will persist through death.
Activation resets Way of the Hunter current sword state.
If this hits an enemy, Yone grants himself a shield for 1.5 seconds, increased by 100% if it hits a champion and by 50% for each subsequent champion hit.
always try to hit a minion first to make sure you start with your mixed damage auto attack.
My first tip is that you can buffer all CC with third Q. What this means is as long as you use third Q as soon as you get CCD, you'll go right through it.
Another thing with Yon Q is that his Q actually has two hit boxes, your tornado and your hitbox. So you can actually hit two people with it by flashing at the end of it.
If you ever wanted to get over a wall like Baron or Dragon Wall and you didn't have third Q, simply E over the wall, Q twice, E back, third Q over to get out of tricky spots
A more advanced tip on Yon is being able to chain Q3 and ult in melee range. The way you fix this is by third queuing and flashing in place to cancel the animation and instantly ult.
if you Q3 and don't have flash to cancel the animation, you can also cancel the animation by queuing into a wall and ending it faster than usual.

A way to fake out your third Q animation and bait out abilities like your W is to use your W when you are right next to someone with third Q. Many times the enemy will panic and blow flash or Vital ability.

Another thing to note about Yon's third Q is that it can actually extend the duration of Yon's E. If you do end up using Yon's third Q to extend the E duration, you can also spam auto attack at the end, even when the E duration wears off to get that one auto up off no matter what.
To guarantee ult landing, you have to land max range Q3 and instantly ult. Make sure to never auto between this combo or they will have time to flash it.
when going for a massive gap close combo, it is far better to lead with ult than Q3 than the opposite
Starting with the basic trading combo with Yon, which is the build Q3, then E, Q3, and auto between all your abilities.
The more people you hit with Yon W, the bigger the shield. That's why it's good to use it after hitting a big ulti to get the biggest shield you can.
If you've ever had Yone jump on you, take half your health and then dash back to safety, this is the combo he used. Charge Q twice, then E to dash forward. Follow with Q3 and auto attack and W,
Land Q3, then immediately cast R. You'll usually E first to close the distance making the setup E Q3 then R.

Then use R to cover a massive distance, pull enemies together, and knock them up. Immediately follow with Q3 to chain another AoE knock up and give your team even more time to follow. A full combo could be E, R, Q3, auto attack W, then continue spamming Q and autos.
Cast E through terrain from fog of war to appear out of nowhere, damage your target, then disappear back behind the wall.
You can also use this to escape over a wall without Q3 ready. E across to a nearby jungle monster, hit it twice with Q, then return and Q3 over the wall.
Begin Q3 just before a root or stun connects. The crowd control will still hit you, but Q3 can continue
Both E and Q3 can dash through terrain, but Q3 travels farther, letting you cross thicker walls to escape or chase enemies who think they're safe.
You can also Q3 into thicker walls you can't cross to cut the dash short. This cancels the long Q3 animation, giving you more time to damage enemies in
With Q3 ready, try using W when you're close to the enemy. They may mistake the animation for your Q3 and waste an important ability, leaving you free to follow with Q3.
Just before it expires, begin casting Q3W or R. Even if the timer runs out, the ability will still finish before E pulls you back, and Q3 can sometimes leave time

Q3 has two separate hit boxes, the tornado and Yone's dash. Send the tornado towards one enemy, then flash into another during the dash to knock up both. At close range, use Q3, then flash in place to cut the dash short and immediately follow with R.
This is for extreme clutch moments, where the 1v1 is everything and you need to cancel the dash animation.
When you have your 3, you put it in and you flash just after the start of the animation, you can actually cancel the end of the Q3 animation and act faster.
Yon's Q3 works a bit like Gragas in the sense that you see when you put it in the air, if you flash on a target, you're going to bump it immediately. In fact, the hitbox is on you
And you also have the possibility of flashing to bump a target that wasn't in the initial position of your 3.
